contracts: analyse(findings: dict) -> tuple[str, list[str]] is the sole public entry point; its return shape is a contract consumed by connector.py at two call sites and must not change without updating both.

Domain-specific investigation guidance (prompts + SPL query templates) lives in splunk/investigation_areas.INVESTIGATION_AREAS, not hardcoded in agent.py's tool bodies — request_deeper_analysis and generate_followup_queries both read from it via get_prompt/get_spl_template.

LogAnalysisState.hypotheses tracks root-cause candidates registered via rank_hypotheses (status starts 'open'); format_report's confirmed_hypothesis arg marks one confirmed and all other open ones rejected. This state is internal to a single analyse() graph invocation only — it does not persist across the outer per-iteration analyse() calls in connector.py's investigation loop.

Tool call arguments (not tool return strings) are the channel for state mutation in tool_node_fn — it reads args from the preceding AIMessage.tool_calls, matched by tool_call_id, rather than parsing sentinel markers out of a tool's return value (format_report's return value is used verbatim as the final report, so it must stay clean).
standalone-agent-langgraph.description: LangGraph ReAct agent (Qwen2.5 via Ollama) used only behind the --investigate CLI flag / connector.py's run_standalone_agent path — the fallback investigation loop for environments without Copilot/Claude driving MCP directly. Reasons over detector findings via a small tool set and emits a markdown report through format_report.
invariants: should_continue ends the loop when iterations >= AGENT_MAX_ITER OR when all tracked hypotheses are resolved (non-'open'), whichever comes first.
Adding a new investigation domain requires only a new entry in INVESTIGATION_AREAS, not edits to agent.py's tool logic.
